title: ArdChangeFeed
description: JSON Schema for one page of the ARD change feed (GET /changes, §5.5): the identifiers a registry added, updated, or removed. A change carries an identifier and nothing about the entry; a consumer fetches the entry from the identifier's authority and confirms every delete there.

Cursor.description: Opaque position in one registry's log, drawn from the unreserved characters of RFC 3986. Consumers compare cursors for equality only and never parse, construct, or order them.

Change.description: One change to the set of identifiers a registry holds.

cursor.description: This change's position, later than the position of every earlier change in the same registry.

op.description: upsert: the registry admitted the entry or its content changed. delete: the registry removed it. A consumer skips an op it does not recognize and still advances its cursor; this enum names the ops defined by this revision.

time.description: When the registry recorded the change, from its own clock. Informational; ordering is by cursor.

identifier.description: The entry's identifier (Appendix C). Its <publisher> segment names the authority the consumer fetches the entry from. Same pattern as the identifier in ard-entry.schema.json.

Change.$comment: additionalProperties is false by design. A change carries no entry content, digest, origin, hop list, or reason; each would create a trust or correctness rule that exists only because a peer's copy of an entry was on the wire. A consumer validating pages from a later revision tolerates an unrecognized op and added members (§5.5.7) rather than treating the page as malformed.

changes.description: Ordered oldest to newest. MAY be empty.

cursor.description: The position up to which the registry had examined its log when it built this page, at or after the last change returned. Present even when changes is empty; passed back as the cursor query parameter.

more.description: true when further changes were available when the page was built; false when the consumer has reached the tail.

retention.description: ISO 8601 duration of the retention window (§5.5.5). Omitted by a registry that retains every change indefinitely and therefore never answers 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED.
